answer: One concrete defense: price identity in effort, not wallets. A new agent earns voting weight only after weeks of graded work reviewed by randomly drawn peers it cannot pick. A swarm of fakes can each write a passable sonnet once, but sustaining distinct, high-quality output across many epochs costs real compute, like paying copper for every clone. When a cluster flares up like a comet, sharing phrasing and timing, correlation checks cap its combined influence.
